Hospital Course:
Mr. Charles Taylor, a 71-year-old male with a history of Type 2 diabetes mellitus, was admitted on November 29, 2011, and has been under regular follow-up for his chronic condition. His most recent visit was on April 1, 2025, for routine management of his diabetes. 

During this visit, Mr. Taylor reported no acute complaints related to his diabetes. He has been compliant with his medication regimen and reports no significant changes in his health status. His diabetes remains well-controlled, as evidenced by his recent A1c levels, which have shown a stable trend over the past year. 

A1c values recorded during his visits are as follows:
- April 1, 2025: A1c 6.2
- September 14, 2024: A1c 6.5
- February 27, 2024: A1c 6.3
- August 12, 2023: A1c 6.4

Mr. Taylor’s vital signs during his latest visit were:
- Blood Pressure: 148/92 mmHg
- Weight: 196 pounds

His physical examination was unremarkable, with no signs of diabetic complications such as retinopathy, neuropathy, or microalbuminuria. He denied any symptoms suggestive of cardiovascular disease.

Social History:
Mr. Taylor reports consuming approximately two alcoholic drinks per week. He has no history of tobacco use. His family history is non-contributory for diabetes or cardiovascular disease.

Discharge Medications:
- Metformin 850 mg twice daily

Discharge Instructions:
Mr. Taylor was advised to continue his current medication regimen and maintain regular follow-up appointments for monitoring of his diabetes. He was encouraged to maintain a healthy diet and engage in regular physical activity, although specific exercise documentation was available during this visit.

Follow-Up:
Mr. Taylor is scheduled for a follow-up appointment in six months to reassess his diabetes control and overall health status. He was instructed to seek medical attention if he experiences any symptoms of hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia, or if he has any concerns regarding his diabetes management.

Additional Notes:
Mr. Taylor’s diabetes has been well-managed over the years with metformin, and he has shown good compliance with his treatment plan. His A1c levels have remained within a target range, indicating effective glycemic control. No

acute interventions or procedures were required during this admission. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue his current management plan.

This discharge summary reflects Mr. Taylor's ongoing care and management of his Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
